put.summary: Register or update a process definition
Apply process definitions to a channel, atomically

post.summary: Compare two sets of process versions: could an instance running one continue under the other, and does the newer one still honour the output contract consumers were written against. It is a shape check — it cannot see a change of meaning such as dollars becoming cents
Validate process definitions and return inferred JSON schemas (no save)
Lease parked external tasks to a worker (FIFO by park time); the returned token is the only handle accepted while the claim is live
Hand a claim back to the queue immediately instead of waiting out its lease

Extend this worker's claims. Answers per token: `renewed` is still yours, `lost` is already someone else's (stop, do not release), `cancelled` is yours but no longer wanted (stop and release). Renewal is mandatory, not an optimisation — it is the only channel that reaches a running worker
Submit an outcome for a waiting external task — a result, or an `error` routed through the task's on_error rules; validated against what the task declares, then the process resumes
Deliver an outcome (result or error) to an external task by instance id + task id: resolves it if armed now, else buffers FIFO until the task next arms

parameters.description: Filter by why a running instance is not executing a task. The three are not one kind of thing: children (blocked until its children settle), collecting (children terminal, their outputs still to merge — runnable now), external (parked until someone answers, or until its timeout). post.summary: Stop a root process instance and its entire descendant tree for good. Terminal and irreversible — unlike pause there is no way back, and a cancelled instance is not retryable. Takes effect at the next task boundary, so a task already executing runs to completion; a claimed external task is told to stop on its next renewal. An assertion: 200 if the tree stopped, 202 if a task already in flight is still draining, 204 if there was nothing live to stop

ignore.description: Members excused from the exit code. Only "contract" is accepted: the upgrade check answers for rows this deployment already owns

passes.description: False only where a gating check broke. Equals compatible when ignore is empty

channel.description: Every process on this channel, at the version the channel points at.

definitions.description: Documents that are not stored yet — the ones an apply would take. They have no version, so they report version null.

versions.description: Process name → version number, or a channel name to resolve it through.

database.description: Storage engine backing this worker: sqlite or postgres

lease_age_ms.description: Milliseconds since this worker last renewed its leases. Past --lease-duration means its claimed instances are being taken over by peers.

manual_tick.description: True when started with -poll 0: the engine only advances via POST /tick

status.description: ok — this worker reached its database; any other outcome is a 503

worker.description: Worker id stamped on the leases this worker holds

instances.description: How many instances in the tree this call wrote

outcome.description: What this call did: applied (the assertion holds and this call made it hold), or accepted (recorded, not yet in effect — a pause left rows draining a task already in flight). A 204 with no body means unchanged: the assertion already held.

status.description: The root instance's status once the write committed

oneOf.description: HTTP call. URL, method, headers and body are all expressions.

items.description: A literal string, or a $: expression / ${ } template evaluated against the context.

anyOf.description: A literal string, or a $: expression / ${ } template evaluated against the context.

accepted_status.description: HTTP status patterns accepted as non-errors, e.g. "2xx" or "404" (defaults to any 2xx). Author it as a literal array (each element a ${ } template or $: expression yielding a string), or as a single $: expression yielding the whole array.

body.description: Templated value building the request body; an object is sent as JSON.

body_schema.description: JSON Schema the body is checked against and conformed to before the request is built. An undeclared key is refused.

additionalProperties.description: A literal string, or a $: expression / ${ } template evaluated against the context.

anyOf.description: A literal string, or a $: expression / ${ } template evaluated against the context.

headers.description: Request headers, evaluating to an object of string values. Author it as a literal map (each value a ${ } template or a $: expression yielding a string), or as a single $: expression yielding the whole map.

method.description: HTTP method, lowercase (e.g. get, post) or a template such as ${ input.method }. Required — the verb is never guessed.

anyOf.description: A literal string, or a $: expression / ${ } template evaluated against the context.

query.description: Query parameters appended to the url, evaluating to an object of scalar values. A null value omits its parameter. Author it as a literal map (each value a ${ } template or a $: expression) or as a single $: expression yielding the whole map.

query_schema.description: JSON Schema the query map is checked against and conformed to. An optional non-nullable parameter fed null is omitted.

responses.description: Status pattern -> JSON Schema for that body. A 2xx key types self.result and accepts the status.

timeout.description: Budget for one attempt, e.g. "30s" (defaults to 30s). A retry gets a fresh budget. Only 'for' applies here — 'until' is external-only.

oneOf.description: Shorthand for 'for', resolved in UTC: "2h30m", a number of milliseconds, or a $: expression.
The long form, naming exactly one of 'for' or 'until' plus an optional 'tz'.

for.description: A duration from when the task is reached: "2h30m", a number of milliseconds, or a $: expression.

tz.description: IANA name ("Europe/Prague") or fixed offset ("+02:00"); defaults to UTC. Abbreviations are rejected.

until.description: An absolute deadline, external tasks only. The same instants as a delay's 'until'.

url.description: Request URL. May contain ${ } interpolations, e.g. ${ config.server_url }/path.

oneOf.description: Single child call: runs one named process and waits. The result is its output, unwrapped.

input.description: Templated value building the child's input payload.

input_schema.description: JSON Schema the input is checked against and conformed to before it is sent. Checkable with no server.

name.description: Name of the child process to invoke.

raises.description: Raise code -> JSON Schema for that code's payload, read as error.data by a rule that catches it.

result_schema.description: JSON Schema validating and exposing the child's output.

version.description: Version to run; 0 means latest published version.

oneOf.description: Keyed child call: named processes run concurrently. The result is keyed by child name.

input.description: Templated value building the child's input payload.

input_schema.description: JSON Schema this entry's input is checked against and conformed to before it is sent.

name.description: Name of the child process to invoke.

raises.description: Raise code -> JSON Schema for that code's payload, declared per entry.

result_schema.description: JSON Schema validating and exposing this child's output.

version.description: Version to run; 0 means latest published version.

children.description: Keyed map of child processes to run concurrently. Keys become the access names in outputs.taskID.

oneOf.description: List fan-out: one child per element of 'over'. The result is an array in 'over' order.

input_schema.description: JSON Schema EACH element is checked against and conformed to before it is sent as one child's input.

name.description: Name of the child process to invoke for every element.

over.description: A $: expression evaluating to an array; one child is spawned per element, with it as input.

raises.description: Raise code -> JSON Schema for that code's payload, read as error.data by a rule that catches it.

result_schema.description: JSON Schema validating and exposing EACH child's output; the result is an array.

version.description: Version to run; 0 means latest published version.

oneOf.description: Delay action: parks the instance until a duration elapses (for) or an instant arrives (until).

for.description: A duration from when the task is reached: "2h30m", a number of milliseconds, or a $: expression.

tz.description: IANA name ("Europe/Prague") or fixed offset ("+02:00"); defaults to UTC. Abbreviations are rejected.

until.description: An instant: RFC 3339, "+2d 08:00", a calendar pattern, unix milliseconds, or a $: expression.

oneOf.description: External task: parks the instance until an outside caller submits a result. No worker is held.

input.description: Templated value snapshotted for the resolver — the only context the queue exposes.

input_schema.description: JSON Schema the input snapshot is checked against and conformed to. It is the contract a worker reads.

raises.description: Code -> JSON Schema for a payload submitted to /external-tasks/fail, read as error.data.

result_schema.description: JSON Schema the submitted result is validated against. Without it any JSON is accepted.

timeout.description: How long to park before raising external.timeout. Omitted, the task waits indefinitely. Takes 'for' or an absolute 'until'.

oneOf.description: Shorthand for 'for', resolved in UTC: "2h30m", a number of milliseconds, or a $: expression.
The long form, naming exactly one of 'for' or 'until' plus an optional 'tz'.

for.description: A duration from when the task is reached: "2h30m", a number of milliseconds, or a $: expression.

tz.description: IANA name ("Europe/Prague") or fixed offset ("+02:00"); defaults to UTC. Abbreviations are rejected.

until.description: An absolute deadline, external tasks only. The same instants as a delay's 'until'.

case.description: Extra condition on the matched error, checked alongside code. A false case falls to the next rule.

code.description: Error code patterns. '%' is the only wildcard; every other character is literal. Empty = catch-all.

goto.description: Task to route to when retries are exhausted. '$task-id' or 'end'. Omit to fail the instance.

not_reached.description: Assert this code means the remote was never reached, so an only_once task may retry it.

panic.description: Terminate as 'failed' with this code and message — a defect. Nothing can catch a panic.

raise.description: Terminate as 'raised' with this code and message — a condition a parent can catch.

retry.description: Retry policy applied before the rule routes. Omit for no retries.

code.description: Error code, lower_snake_case with no dots. A literal — never an expression.

data.description: Structured payload this fault carries, evaluated when the clause fires. Lands on error.data.

message.description: Human-readable message. A template: ${ } renders when the clause fires.

config_schema.description: Flat object of primitive config variables, resolved from the server environment and read as config.<NAME>.

input_schema.description: JSON Schema used to validate the input payload when starting a new instance.

output.description: Templated value evaluated at completion to produce the process output.

output_schema.description: JSON Schema the process output is checked against and conformed to. Declared, it is what this process publishes.

tasks.description: Ordered list of execution tasks. Control advances linearly unless a switch case redirects.

oneOf.description: Shorthand for 'retries', on the default backoff curve (1s, doubling, capped at 5m).
The long form: retry count plus any part of the backoff curve. Every slot takes a $: expression.

delay.description: Wait before the first retry: "30s", a number of milliseconds, or a $: expression. Defaults to 1s.

factor.description: Multiplier applied to the wait after each attempt. 1 keeps it constant. Defaults to 2.

max_delay.description: Ceiling the growing wait is clamped to. Defaults to 5m, or to 'delay' when that is longer.

retries.description: Number of retries before following goto or failing. 0 = no retries.

anyOf.description: A $: typed expression, a ${ } interpolation template, or a literal string.
Literal array; each element is recursively a Shape.
Literal object; each value is recursively a Shape.

oneOf.description: Ordered routing rules; first match wins and the last must be a catch-all (omit 'case').

case.description: Boolean expression. Omit for a catch-all; must be last.

goto.description: "end" to terminate, "next" to advance, or "$task-id" to jump to a task.

panic.description: Terminate as 'failed' with this code and message — a defect. Nothing can catch a panic.

raise.description: Terminate as 'raised' with this code and message — a condition a parent can catch.

action.description: Describes the action to perform. Omit for switch-only (routing) tasks.

id.description: Task identifier, unique within the definition.

on_error.description: Ordered error-routing rules evaluated when the call fails. First match wins.

only_once.description: At-most-once execution: only errors that never reached the remote may retry. Defaults to false.

output.description: Templated value remapping this task's output; it becomes outputs.taskID and self.output.

output_schema.description: JSON Schema this task's output is checked against and conformed to. It becomes the published type of outputs.taskID.

switch.description: Required. Routing: a shorthand ("next", "end", "$task-id") or an ordered list of cases.

default.description: The value used when this one is absent. Annotation only — it does not make a required property optional.

description.description: Free text. Shown in the editor, and never a constraint.

enum.description: The complete set of values allowed here.

items.description: The schema every element of an array conforms to.

oneOf.description: The value conforms to exactly one of these schemas.

properties.description: The named members of an object, each a schema.

required.description: Which properties must be present. A property not listed here may be absent, and reading it yields null.

secret.description: Redacts the value from logs. Only meaningful in a process config_schema.

type.description: The value's JSON type, or a list of types it may take.
